frames.narration: The release train cuts version 7 from one commit. CI builds and signs the iOS and Android builds with keys from the secrets store, and submits them to the stores as build 7.0.0. Store review takes a day. The new feed feature ships switched off.
Review passes and the store releases to 1% of users. A phone that updates opens the app and fetches config, which turns new-feed on for 1% of v7 users.

Every request carries the app version. The gateway reads 7.0.0 and gives it the new response shape; a v5 phone asking for the same screen gets the old shape, so nothing breaks for the versions still in use.
By the next day 2,400 users have v7. Their phones upload crash reports tagged with the version. Crashes are 3.5% of v7 users against 0.5% of v6 users, and the new-feed screen is behind most of them.

The gate has its minimum of 2,000 users on v7. It compares the two rates, sees a gap well beyond the noise margin, halts the staged rollout at 1% and pages a person. About 2,400 people have v7, and nobody else will get it.
The crash is inside the new feed, so the gate also flips its flag. Phones read the change the next time the app opens, within about a day, and stop crashing without any store review or update.

A second bug is found in code that has no flag. First a server-side mitigation: the gateway stops sending the field that triggers it to 7.0.0. Then the hotfix 7.0.1 is built from the released commit and submitted with a request for expedited review.

7.0.1 is released to everyone at once. A phone on v4 that skipped two updates installs it and its on-device database runs the three pending migrations in order inside one transaction. About a quarter of the remaining v7 users update each day; the few who switched updates off stay on 7.0.0, still protected by the server.
